pink-roadhouse-oodnadatta.name: Pink Roadhouse
pink-roadhouse-oodnadatta.bio: Pink roadhouse in Oodnadatta, the Oodnadatta Track's fuel stop, post office and information hub.
notes: Free to stop; meals and fuel are paid extras. Site pinkroadhouse.com.au title 'The Pink Roadhouse - On the Oonadatta Track' (sic).

railway-tjukurpa-museum.name: Railway Tjukurpa Museum
railway-tjukurpa-museum.bio: Museum in Oodnadatta's old Ghan railway station; the key is collected from the Pink Roadhouse.
railway-tjukurpa-museum.ticket_note: No official site found; run by the community, key held at the Pink Roadhouse.
railway-tjukurpa-museum.coordinates_source: OSM tourism=museum 'Oodnadatta Railway Station Museum' (Nominatim); Wikivoyage listing -27.546114,135.447715 is 18 m away (HIGH)
notes: No fee found in any source; marked free but unverified. Key from Pink Roadhouse or Transcontinental Hotel.

marree.name: Marree
marree.bio: Outback railway town at the start of the Birdsville and Oodnadatta Tracks, with the historic Marree Hotel.
marree.coordinates_source: OSM boundary=administrative centre via resolve-pin (MEDIUM); Commons main-street photos at -29.64703,138.0631
notes: Town as a draw per Wikivoyage and Flinders & Outback.

marree-mosque.name: Marree Mosque
marree-mosque.bio: A 2003 recreation of Australia's first mosque, a mud-brick building raised by Afghan cameleers around 1882.
marree-mosque.coordinates_source: OSM building=ruins 'Marree Mosque' (Nominatim); Commons photo of the 1884 mosque at -29.6455,138.063 agrees (HIGH). Wikipedia's -29.651346 is 650 m south and was not used
notes: OSM tags the site as ruins and Wikipedia calls it a former mosque; Wikivoyage says a recreation used by the local Afghan community. Visitors see it from outside. Worth confirming access.

mungerannie-hotel.name: Mungerannie Hotel
mungerannie-hotel.bio: Outback pub on the Birdsville Track, its bar ceiling covered in stockmen's hats and other memorabilia.
mungerannie-hotel.ticket_note: Official domain mungeranniehotel.com.au is unconfirmed (new owners; site may have changed); see needs_browser.
notes: Renamed from 'Mungerannie' (draft) to the pub it is; icon changed. Free to stop; drinks, meals, camping are paid extras.

andamooka.name: Andamooka
andamooka.bio: Opal-mining village near Roxby Downs where visitors can noodle for opal on the old mullock heaps.
notes: Fossicking: never on registered claims. Andamooka Observatory runs paid noodling tours (not priced here).

arid-recovery-reserve.name: Arid Recovery Reserve
arid-recovery-reserve.bio: Fenced desert reserve north of Roxby Downs where rare native species are seen on sunset tours.
arid-recovery-reserve.coordinates_source: LOW: approximate point on Borefield Road at Olympic Dam (OSM highway); the tour gate is 12 km along Borefield Road from Olympic Way per Roxby Downs Council, no gate coordinates found
notes: pin: LOW. Adult (16+) $100 plus booking fees, child $50, from aridrecovery.org.au/visit/tours; 2.5 h, Fridays April-October (extra Wednesdays in school holidays). Booked through Roxby Downs Visitor Information Centre.

woomera-missile-park.name: Woomera Missile Park
woomera-missile-park.bio: Open-air display of missiles and rockets developed at the Woomera range, in a park in the town centre.
woomera-missile-park.ticket_note: Town-run open park, no official page.
woomera-missile-park.coordinates_source: Median of 5 geotagged Commons 'Woomera Missile Park' files (spread ~40 m); Wikivoyage places it at Banool and Dewrang Avenues (MEDIUM)
notes: Single-source point; no OSM feature found.

woomera-heritage-centre.name: Woomera Heritage Centre
woomera-heritage-centre.bio: Museum in Woomera's heritage and visitor centre on the history of the Rocket Range.
woomera-heritage-centre.ticket_note: woomera.com.au answers 200 on every path with a splash page, so unconfirmed; needs browser.
woomera-heritage-centre.coordinates_source: OSM tourism=information 'Woomera Heritage and Visitor Information Centre', Dewrang Avenue (Photon) (MEDIUM)
notes: Price conflicts: Wikivoyage $6, an older listing $3 adult. $6 used; unverified.

lake-hart.name: Lake Hart
lake-hart.bio: Salt lake beside the Stuart Highway, seen pink from the roadside Lake Hart Lookout.
lake-hart.coordinates_source: OSM 'Lake Hart Lookout' (tourism=camp_site / amenity=shelter) on the Stuart Highway (Nominatim) (MEDIUM); the lake itself is at -31.144,136.385
notes: Lake lies within the Woomera Test Range; only the highway lookout is a public stop. Wikipedia title 'Lake Hart (South Australia)' does not exist (redlink), so wiki omitted. 'Pink' per southaustralia.com; colour varies with season.
